pages.reference_note: Read-from-image: page is an Erasmus 'Formulae' printing (header 'ORVM FORMVLAE PER ERAS. 27', Roman-type, 'uis/uiri' u-spelling, CHR./AVG. speaker tags) with heavy MANUSCRIPT marginalia ('Culpa est eius q[ui] nescius aliquem læsit', 'Causa proprie d[icitu]r id ex quo...', 'Mora est expectatio uel temporis dilatio'). The reference is from a DIFFERENT setting: different lineation, v-spelling ('vis', 'vtendum'), speaker written 'Christianus'/'August.', 'queso' for 'quæso', a typo 'studiolissimus', and it starts with a sentence from the previous page ('Uis me tibi morem gerere?') and ends with 'Quo minus' from the next. It has no header and no handwritten notes. Floor CER is ~0.14 even for a perfect read.

per_engine.gemini-3.1-flash-lite: Good main text, but long-s read as f ('Differe' for 'Diſſere', 'fo te' for 'ſo te'), 'EKAS' in the header, drops macrons ('quide'); it transcribes the handwriting loosely ('appertatio', 'lesu').
per_engine.lite+longs: Same read as lite with ſ restored. 'Diſſere' is now right, but the header still says 'EKAS'.
per_engine.gemini-3-flash-preview: Main text is clean, but it modernises ſ→s and reads 'Differe' (long-s→f). It interleaves the handwritten notes into the printed lines ('uaco Culpa est eius q').
per_engine.flash+cal: Same as flash-preview with ſ restored, but it adds a doubled abbreviation mark 'utriq;;'.
per_engine.gemini-3.8-flash: Most faithful read: ſ, tildes ('obſecũdem', 'quidẽ', 'grãmatice'), header 'ERAS'. It puts the manuscript notes in a separate block after the text and reads 'expectatio' (right) where the others have 'appellatio' or 'appertatio'.
per_engine.gemini-3.1-pro-preview: Equally accurate on the print ('utriqʒ', 'quidẽ'), but it splices the handwritten notes into the printed lines.
per_engine.glm-ocr: Lowest CER (0.143), but only because it drops the header and most of the manuscript notes, which the reference also lacks. Real errors: 'priuscj' for 'priuſq̃', 'studioissimus', 'grámatice quidé', modern s throughout.
per_engine.calamari-gt4histocr-bin: Good on the printed body (ſ, ẽ, ũ), but the header is garbage ('ORVAE D EAS') and it emits noise for the handwriting ('eeer cſcius liue', 'Mana petl0 uα xpοri').

pages.summary: Every CER here is dominated by an edition mismatch: the reference is a different setting, with v/u spelling, expanded speaker names and spill from the neighbouring pages, and the image has handwritten notes the reference lacks. All Gemini arms read the print nearly perfectly, and they score worse than GLM only because they also transcribe the header and the handwriting. The CER ranking is a reference artefact, not an accuracy signal.

pages.reference_note: Read-from-image: a Judith drama page in italic verse ('296 IVDITH.', Scena VII), with a roman marginal note at left ('Dux & chiliarchę mirãtur eius uenuſtatẽ...'). The reference has the right text but in NORMALISED spelling (v for u, ae for æ, 'feminas' for 'fœminas', 'auctoritas'-style), and it adds a line from the previous page ('et elegantiae decus tuae') and words from the next ('per imperium nomen'). It places the marginal note after the scene heading. Usable, but the floor is about 0.05. The image also shows the facing page's gutter strip at right.

per_engine.gemini-3.1-flash-lite: Accurate. The marginal note comes after the heading, matching the reference order. Long-s→f errors ('Luftrato, quis fit'), 'quamum' for 'quantum'.
per_engine.lite+longs: Same as lite with ſ fixed ('Luſtrato, quis ſit'). One of the two lowest CERs (0.06).
per_engine.gemini-3-flash-preview: The text is right, but it moves the marginal note to the END of the page. That reordering alone costs about 0.15 CER, so this is an order artefact, not a misread.
per_engine.flash+cal: Same as flash-preview (marginal note at the end, 0.215), plus doubled 'atq;;'.
per_engine.gemini-3.8-flash: Marginal note in reading order, ſ and tildes kept ('mirã-', 'ſtatẽ'). One real misread: 'quam uir' for 'quantum'.
per_engine.gemini-3.1-pro-preview: Transcribes the gutter strip of the FACING page ('io, per', 'Arabi', 'ſtrág;', 'impera', 'liberun'...) as a second column interleaved line by line. That bleed from the neighbouring page is the cause of the 0.352 CER, and it also reads 'quam uim'.
per_engine.glm-ocr: Omits the marginal note entirely, which accounts for most of the 0.155. Also misreads: 'ucni', 'lumuna', 'delecstat', 'uirus', 'dominier', 'Nobis¢'.
per_engine.calamari-gt4histocr-bin: Splices the marginal note into the scene heading and verse lines, garbles the drop-cap line ('Voſepius ... lumna'), 'not.' for 'HOL.'. It is the only engine to get the folio right ('296'; the Gemini arms say 295).

pages.summary: Text quality is high for all the LLM arms. The CER spread of 0.06 to 0.35 comes from LAYOUT, not misreading: where the marginal note is placed (flash-preview puts it at the end) and whether the facing page's gutter is read (pro). Gemini-3.8-flash and lite+longs read this page best.

pages.reference_note: Read-from-image: a folio of 'De rebus gestis lib. IV' p.101 (Orchanes, 1335), with printed side-notes ('Orchanes Turcarum Imperator', 'Venetorũ & Genuẽſium diſcordiæ obſunt', 'Christianorum motus') and a handwritten note at the bottom right ('Rodolphus de Masmünster prior ...'). The reference is itself an uncorrected OCR text: 'ambitlone', 'audaeia', 'patemum', 'cirea', 'Orchanesi'. It also adds the previous page's last line ('rerum Asianarum Christianis nihil superesset.') and the next page's opening ('1345. Hugone mortuo, Petrus'). The floor is about 0.05.

per_engine.lite+longs: Most ſ restored, but some f survive ('tranfgreffus', 'fuu'). 0.088.
per_engine.gemini-3-flash-preview: Clean text, with the side-notes collected at the end. Base output has f for ſ ('abfimilis', 'ftrenue', 'Burfiam').
per_engine.flash+cal: ſ fixed. Side-notes at the end. Doubled 'atq;;'. 0.082.
per_engine.gemini-3.8-flash: Systematic error: every i is rendered as í ('ením Ottomanní fílíus', 'vírtutís'), which doubles its CER to 0.211. It also reads 1335 as '1315' and keeps f for ſ in places ('abfímílís').
per_engine.gemini-3.1-pro-preview: Faithful: ſ, tildes ('ſuũ', 'Græcorũ', 'Hẽnenberg'), 'ſtrenuè', side-notes inline, and it reads the handwriting as 'Rodolphus de Maſmünſter prior ꝑ Alem'.
per_engine.glm-ocr: Lowest CER (0.07) because it reflows to prose and skips the folio and some side-notes. Errors: 'opulenior', 'decederer', 'reličis', 'apparatuç'.
per_engine.calamari-gt4histocr-bin: Most lines good, but it collapses one line to junk ('Terſſgr Ponum imperim ſut pro? nperao.'), reads the date as 'ijz5' and the handwriting as 'odelp  Al'.

pages.summary: The reference is a noisy OCR, so every engine's floor is about 0.05 and GLM 'wins' partly by omission. The real outlier is gemini-3.8-flash, with a page-wide i→í substitution: that is a genuine engine defect, not a reference artefact. By eye, Pro reads this page best, with flash+cal next.

pages.reference_note: Read-from-image: a short italic page with a 3-line epigram ('Laternam tamen obruiſtis vnam: ...') and a 5-line note on the deaths of Zwingli and Oecolampadius ending 'anno ætatis XLIX.'. Strong mirrored show-through is visible, including 'IOANNI OECOLAMPADIO.' and a verse block. The reference PREPENDS 'malae, lucernam,' (from the previous page) and TRUNCATES the last line: it ends at 'Cal. Decembris' and lacks 'anno ætatis XLIX'. On a page this short (about 290 characters), these two errors alone give a floor of about 0.11.

per_engine.gemini-3.1-flash-lite: Text right apart from f-for-ſ ('obruiftis', 'fepulta', 'Ipfa fed'). It ADDS 'IOANNI OECOLAMPADIO.' and 'M', read from the mirrored SHOW-THROUGH.
per_engine.lite+longs: ſ fixed except 'Ipfa'. Same show-through insertion of 'IOANNI OECOLAMPADIO. M'.
per_engine.gemini-3-flash-preview: Text perfect, but it also transcribes the show-through title 'IOANNI OECOLAMPADIO.' and 'M'. That insertion is the gap from 0.116 to 0.199.
per_engine.flash+cal: Identical to flash-preview, including the show-through insertion.
per_engine.gemini-3.8-flash: Perfect transcription with no show-through. Its 0.116 is entirely the reference's prepended and truncated text.
per_engine.gemini-3.1-pro-preview: Perfect transcription with no show-through, same 0.116 floor. Tied with 3.8-flash.
per_engine.glm-ocr: Reads the show-through title, plus misreads: 'nam' for 'vnam', 'Oetobris', 'obit', 'vita'/'atatis' (dropped æ), and spaced numerals 'X L I I I I'.
per_engine.calamari-gt4histocr-bin: Drops initials and numerals: 'uinglius', 'I I.' for 'XLIIII', 'al.' for 'Cal.', 'ætatis  I.' for 'XLIX', 'Iſa' for 'Ipſa'.

pages.summary: Pro and 3.8-flash are letter-perfect, and their 0.116 is pure reference error (neighbour-page prefix and truncated last line). Lite and flash-preview lose about 0.08 by transcribing the mirrored show-through heading. GLM and Calamari make real reading errors.

pages.reference_note: Read-from-image: a dialogue drama in roman type ('SECVNDVS', MER./PA./CON. speakers, 'autoritas', 'Vt', 'Cœcus cœcis', catchword 'D 4 CON.'). The reference is the right text NORMALISED: 'auctoritas' for 'autoritas', 'Ut' for 'Vt', 'Coecus' for 'Cœcus', 'et' for '&'. It joins the turn-overs ('(satis', '(te.') into their lines, adds two lines from the previous page ('Sacrilegos patres...defensitant.') and the next page's opening ('CON. Tuo inquam, cuius'). The floor is about 0.10 for everyone.

per_engine.gemini-3.1-flash-lite: Long-s→f everywhere ('fi fexcenti', 'effe', 'fedulò'). This adds about 0.05 over the other arms (0.155).
per_engine.lite+longs: ſ restored. At the common floor (0.107). Reads 'Cæcus' where the image has 'Cœcus'.
per_engine.gemini-3-flash-preview: Modernises ſ→s and 'Ut' for 'Vt'. Otherwise accurate. At the floor.
per_engine.gemini-3.8-flash: Accurate, but it letter-spaces small caps ('M E R.', 'C H R I S T I'), which costs a few characters. Reads 'tū' for 'tu'.
per_engine.gemini-3.1-pro-preview: Most faithful: 'Cœcus cœcis' (œ as printed), 'absq́ue', ſ throughout. At the floor (0.105).
per_engine.glm-ocr: Near the floor, but with real misreads: 'emerississes', 'cenles', 'Fortaissis'.
per_engine.calamari-gt4histocr-bin: Body good. Spaced small caps garbled ('CnRIITTI', 'ME .', 'Mr.', 'Co.'), 'eœcis', 'cœcnm'.

pages.summary: All arms except base lite sit at the same 0.105–0.114 floor, set by the reference's normalised spelling and its neighbour-page lines. Base lite's extra 0.05 is genuine long-s→f. By eye, Pro is the most faithful (œ, ſ), but the differences are tiny.

pages.reference_note: Read-from-image: Newton, Principia (1687) p.[94], 'Schol.', with a diagram (circle, letters P, L, N, M, H, K, C, B, G, O) and text wrapped around it. The reference (Wikisource) matches the text. Its small artefacts are a prefix from the previous page ('Prob. XIV. Trajectoriam describere. Q.E.F.'), 'illa altera' from the next page, and 'q;' expanded to 'que' on its own line. The floor is about 0.04.

per_engine.gemini-3.1-flash-lite: Reflowed paragraphs, essentially perfect. One long-s→f ('fas fit').
per_engine.lite+longs: Letter-perfect as far as I can see ('aliæq;', 'atq;', ſ throughout). 0.040.
per_engine.gemini-3-flash-preview: REFUSED, with empty output. This is probably a recitation block on a famous text (Newton), not a reading failure.
per_engine.gemini-3.8-flash: Line-preserving and accurate, but it mixes s and f for ſ ('diftantes', 'diftans' next to 'Asymptoti').
per_engine.calamari-gt4histocr-bin: Good body text. Misses the bracket '(', reads 'Poſiquam', 'IBXGC' for 'IBKGC', drops 'K vel k', and emits stray diagram letters ('7', 'i').

pages.summary: A clean page with a sound reference, where every working engine sits at 0.04 and the remaining CER is reference framing. The notable failure is the flash-preview refusal on Newton's Principia (also inherited by flash+cal). By eye, lite+longs is best and 3.8-flash second (s/f mixing).

pages.reference_note: Read-from-image: '30 De Fermentatione.', a dense roman text on the spleen, with catchword 'fermenteſcit'. The FACING page's left edge, with partial words (31, 'menteſ-', 'pochon-'...), is visible at right. The reference matches. Its artefacts are a prefix from the previous page ('vilissimi reputatur, ut sit tantum'), no catchword, and modern s. The floor is about 0.02.

per_engine.gemini-3.1-flash-lite: Accurate except systematic long-s→f ('five fentina', 'fanguinis', 'ftructuræ'), which accounts for its 0.072.
per_engine.gemini-3-flash-preview: The page text is excellent, but it then transcribes the FACING page's cropped column ('31 / menteſ- / pochon- / ſo tume- / deſtitui- ...', about 35 lines). That neighbouring-page bleed is the whole 0.163.
per_engine.gemini-3.8-flash: Line-preserving, ſ throughout, no bleed. It swaps the header order ('De Fermentatione. / 30') and reads 'fæculentiæ' where the print has œ. 0.024.

pages.summary: A clean page and a good reference, where four engines tie at about 0.025. Flash-preview and flash+cal's 0.163 is entirely transcription of the facing page's cropped edge, a real failure (bleed from the neighbouring page). Base lite's 0.072 is long-s→f. 3.8-flash and Calamari read best.

pages.reference_note: Read-from-image: 'Lectiones in Acta Apostolorum' p.59, with about 10 lines of GREEK in ligature-heavy type (Chrysostom 'Λιβερτῖνοι δὲ...', Philo 'Πῶς οὖν ἀπεδέχετο...'), the Greek inline in Latin text. The reference DELETES ALL GREEK (left as ' , ' / ' . '). It also drops 'accessisse' and 'vitâ' ('in Ciceronis'), and adds the previous page's tail ('discipuli non tantùm ad Templum') and the next page's opening ('quos Ptolemaeus Lagi'). About 25–30% of the printed characters have no counterpart in the reference.

per_engine.gemini-3.1-flash-lite: Latin fine apart from f-for-ſ ('acceffiffe', 'fed'). Greek mostly right but with slips ('ὕτω καλεῖται', 'ἰδάζασθαι' for 'παραχαράξαι'), and 'illis' for 'illic'.
per_engine.lite+longs: Same as lite with ſ. Every correctly read Greek character counts as an insertion against the reference (0.297).
per_engine.gemini-3-flash-preview: Best Greek: 'οὕτω καλοῦνται', 'πλείους', 'παραχαράξαι βιασθέντες', with the ου-ligatures expanded. Latin clean ('Qui illic', 'Maccabæorum'). Its 0.30 is the stripped-Greek artefact.
per_engine.gemini-3.8-flash: Greek rendered diplomatically but partly wrong ('ὕτω καλεῖται', 'ἐδὲν', 'Ἰεδαίων'). Latin excellent.
per_engine.glm-ocr: Greek degenerates into a REPETITION LOOP ('ἀπελύγεροι τῶν πέγεων τὸ Τιβέρρεως ποταμίωι μεγάλην' repeated to 6.5k characters). That loop is the 3.509 CER.
per_engine.calamari-gt4histocr-bin: Latin good. Greek is unreadable noise ('AGei ,è, P P ω', 'Iſs Vν πε ) τυ'). It gets the LOWEST CER (0.173) only because its garbage is shorter than real Greek and the reference has no Greek.

pages.summary: The CER ranking is inverted by the reference: it omits all Greek, so engines that read the Greek correctly (Gemini, about 0.30) score worse than Calamari, whose Greek is noise (0.17). GLM's 3.5 is a genuine repetition loop on Greek. By eye, flash-preview and flash+cal read the Greek best, and 3.8-flash's Latin is equal but its Greek is worse.

pages.reference_note: Read-from-image: 'minimorum animalium Theatrum' p.15 (on bees). The page is photographed CURVED, so lines bow at the left, and it has a Greek list of words for beehives ('κυψέλας, σίμβλους, ...κελέβας'). The reference has the Latin right but OMITS that Greek list, adds a line from the previous page ('arctè obdormiscit. Exercitatio apum duplex est, altera') and words from the next ('tectis apes includunt affabre'). Lightly affected; the floor is about 0.05.

per_engine.gemini-3.1-flash-lite: Long-s→f ('anhelofæ', 'falutis', 'fupereffe'), 'alijsfue', 'offenflores'. It also normalises 'appellitant' to 'appellant', as all the Gemini arms do.
per_engine.lite+longs: Most ſ fixed, some f left ('folo externa fefe', 'fufpenfas'). 'offenflores'.
per_engine.gemini-3-flash-preview: Cleanest: correct 'offensiores', a plausible Greek list ('κυψέλας, σίμβλους, ... κελέβας'). But 'alijsque' for 'alijſue', 'appellant' for 'appellitant', and ſ→s.
per_engine.flash+cal: Same as flash-preview, with ſ re-added inconsistently (s and ſ mixed).
per_engine.gemini-3.8-flash: Line-faithful ('alijſue', 'aggrediamùr'), but it mixes f and ſ ('neceffitatis', 'falutis'), has 'iri ædibus', and its Greek is garbled ('κοΐαρυς', 'πυέλσκυς').
per_engine.glm-ocr: The Latin is fine, but on the Greek list it falls into a REPETITION LOOP ('κυσίδας, κυσίδας, ...'), doubling its length to 7.4k. That loop is the 0.751 CER.
per_engine.calamari-gt4histocr-bin: Handles the curved lines decently but loses initials ('amen', 'ſmo', 'lolo', 'etergunt'). Greek is noise. Keeps 'appellitant' correctly.

pages.summary: A good reference except for the omitted Greek list. Gemini arms sit at 0.055–0.09, with the differences driven by long-s→f in lite and 3.8-flash. GLM's 0.75 is a real repetition loop on Greek. All Gemini arms silently 'correct' the rare word 'appellitant' to 'appellant', a small normalisation error the CER hardly sees. By eye, flash-preview is best.

pages.reference_note: Read-from-image: 'Lectiones in Acta Apostolorum' p.57, the same book as p93. About 40% of the page is GREEK (Josephus 'Καθίζει συνέδριον κριτῶν...', Hegesippus, Origen, Clement, Eusebius quotations). The reference DELETES ALL GREEK and also drops 'Hegesippus' once ('. lib. 5.'). It adds the previous page's tail ('Apostolis Ordinatur Jacobus... ex traditione') and the next page's opening ('IV. Quis autem hic Jacobus'). The reference is unusable for scoring this page; a perfect read scores about 0.5.

per_engine.gemini-3.1-flash-lite: Greek fluent but with substitutions: 'ἀγαγὼν' for 'παραγαγὼν', 'τρόπον' for 'θρόνον' (the print shows 'θρόνον'). Latin has f-for-ſ ('Apoftolorum', 'exiftat').
per_engine.gemini-3-flash-preview: Greek matches the print closely ('καὶ παραγαγὼν', 'ὀνομασθεὶς', 'μέχρι καὶ ἡμῶν', 'θρόνον'), with ligatures expanded. Latin clean. Its 0.559 is the stripped-Greek artefact. Caveat: a fluent Greek read can also come from the model's memory of these famous quotations (Eusebius 'δὲ δὴ αὐτὸν' is uncertain against the ligature in the print).
per_engine.gemini-3.8-flash: Same quality as flash-preview, and it preserves line breaks. Eusebius line rendered 'δὲ καὶ αὐτὸν'. Latin perfect.
per_engine.glm-ocr: Hallucinated Greek: recycled phrases ('ἐν ἀρχαγαγών οἰσμμα αὐτὰ', 'λιχηφόρετον ἐλέδου') repeated across the quotations. Latin slips: 'alterat', 'appellâtet'.
per_engine.calamari-gt4histocr-bin: Latin very good. Greek is pure noise ('Kaiu σuiio xpι', 'IdC Ci τ'). LOWEST CER (0.318) only because its noise is shorter than real Greek.

pages.summary: The worst reference in the set: it omits about 40% of the page (all the Greek), so the CERs of 0.5–0.6 measure the reference, not the engines, and the ranking is inverted (Calamari's Greek noise 'wins'). By eye, flash-preview and 3.8-flash read the page best; lite substitutes Greek words, and GLM invents Greek.

pages.reference_note: Read-from-image: 'Cometarum Natura' p.27, roman with italics, a brace diagram ('Solem eſſe fixum / Alia eſſe vel eſſe poſſe Syſtemata... / Mundum eſſe immenſum'), quotation marks in the margin, catchword 'lem'. The reference (EEBO-TCP style) matches the text. Its artefacts are a line from the previous page ('Saxum sudat nitendo neque proficit'), 'q;' expanded to 'que' on its own line, and modern s. The floor is about 0.02.

per_engine.gemini-3.1-flash-lite: Accurate, but with systematic long-s→f ('ipfa', 'fine', 'Afferere poffit iftam'), hence 0.087.
per_engine.gemini-3-flash-preview: The cleanest read: ſ throughout, marginal quotation marks kept, 0.020.
per_engine.flash+cal: Same as flash-preview, but the calibration step doubles every 'q;' to 'q;;' ('atq;;', 'eorumq;;'), which raises it to 0.033. This is an arm artefact.
per_engine.gemini-3.8-flash: Accurate, but the first lines keep f for ſ ('ipfa', 'Afferere poffit iftam'), then switch to ſ.
per_engine.calamari-gt4histocr-bin: Good, but it drops accents and abbreviation marks ('Certe multum', 'depulſa Anomali', 'verum') and garbles small bits ('ei hilum', 'mor tus', 'ſor').

pages.summary: A clean page with a good reference, and all engines read it well. The differences are long-s→f (base lite; the start of 3.8-flash's page) and flash+cal's doubled 'q;;'. Flash-preview is best by eye and by CER.
